correctness.rationale: The exact q-fold root-of-unity sum kills all cross-residue Gram entries. Each surviving block is a single symmetric-window Fourier Gram matrix with beta=q alpha. The exterior power of its convergent Fourier Taylor operator has unique lowest-degree nonzero wedge indexed 0,...,j; the leading wedge norm is the product of consecutive Vandermonde and monomial Gram determinants. Dividing consecutive exterior-power asymptotics and using the squared monic Legendre norm produces every c_(r,j)>0. This proves the full spectrum for each fixed finite mask, exact tightness with no residue collisions, and the sharp condition number; the six-mode example and 134 independent numerical assertions corroborate without replacing proof.

value.rationale: For a natural measurement system consisting of q periodic observation gates and an arbitrary sparse integer frequency mask, the theorem computes every sharp singular-value decay exponent and coefficient, rather than only a rate or an isolated example. Congruence-class multiplicities provide a concise observable rank/stability invariant, exact tightness classification, and precise worst-mode noise-amplification rate. The formulas permit direct evaluation of any fixed sparse mask and distinguish stable collision-free sampling from severe clustering, with applications to Fourier observability and gated sensing. No broader finite-width or perturbed-aperture design theorem is claimed.
